Principle 02 of 8

Autonomy

People choose freely and knowingly, and can say no, change their mind, or leave.

Protects

Customers, users, workers

Why it matters

A choice that was engineered, hidden, or made impossible to undo is not a real choice.

Covers

Subscriptions, contracts, and lock-in (Category 2), misdirection, obstruction, and forced action (3.3–3.5), and consent manipulation (5.1).

1.9 Tipping Manipulation · 3 practices

Autonomy+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
1.9.1Pre-Selected Default Tip PercentagesPOS terminals defaulting to high tip percentages (often 18–30%), placing the no-tip option in a smaller, lower-contrast, or extra-tap location, or pre-highlighting the largest amount.Counter-service food, retail, mobile POS systems, ride-hailing apps
1.9.2Tip Solicitation Outside Service ContextsSoliciting tips in transactions historically not tipped — self-checkout, take-out, retail, automated kiosks — exploiting social pressure and unfamiliarity to extract gratuities for services that involve no traditional service component.Retail, self-checkout, automated kiosks, take-out food, airport concessions
1.9.3Tip-on-Tax / Tip-on-Pre-Discount TotalCalculating suggested tip percentages on the tax-inclusive total or pre-discount price, inflating the displayed "suggested" amount above the cost of the underlying service.Restaurants, food delivery, hospitality

2.1 Cancellation Friction (Roach Motel) · 5 practices

Autonomy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
2.1.1Asymmetric Signup/CancelAllowing instant online signup while requiring phone calls, certified mail, or in-person visits to cancel.Fitness/gyms, dating, gambling, cosmetics, cleaning, mental health, telecom
2.1.2Cancellation MazeDesigning multi-step cancellation flows with confusing portals, hidden links, or repeated confirmation steps.Fitness, dating, mobile carriers, food delivery, streaming, dental insurance
2.1.3Retention Dark PatternsMandatory retention calls, guilt-tripping prompts, repeated "are you sure?" friction, or hidden cancel buttons that pressure users to stay.Streaming, fitness, cybersecurity, mental health, news subscriptions
2.1.4Zombie Billing Post-CancelContinuing to charge after a cancellation has been requested, citing "processing periods" or "billing-cycle completion."Fitness, dating, cleaning, telecom
2.1.5Cooling-Off Period RemovalEliminating any post-sale cancellation window even when the user has not yet used the service.Telecom, fitness, real estate (leases), wedding planning

Autonomy+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
2.2.1Hidden RenewalAuto-renewing subscriptions or contracts without prominent advance notice, banking on user inattention.Streaming, telecom, fitness, dating, supplements, pest control, waste management
2.2.2Free-Trial Conversion TrapCollecting payment information for "free" trials and silently converting to paid at the end of the trial without notification.Streaming, cosmetics, supplements, software, dating
2.2.3Auto-Renewal with EscalationAutomatically renewing into a new long-term commitment at a higher price or expanded scope without affirmative consent.Cleaning services, waste management, fitness, telecom
2.2.4Renewal Pressure TacticsUsing urgency, fear messaging, or artificial deadlines at renewal to upgrade or rebind.Insurance, cybersecurity, supplements
2.2.5Silent Coverage ErosionRenewing policies or contracts with reduced coverage at the same or higher price without highlighting the changes.Insurance, cloud/SaaS, telecom

2.3 Tier Degradation & Feature Gating · 8 practices

Autonomy+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
2.3.1Tier DegradationMoving features previously included in a tier to a higher-priced tier (or removing them altogether).Streaming, SaaS, gaming, home appliances
2.3.2Feature Gating of Existing HardwareSoftware-disabling capabilities present in already-purchased hardware to justify a premium tier.Home appliances, automotive (over-the-air feature removal), connected devices
2.3.3Subscription Requirements for Core FunctionsRequiring ongoing payment for features that were one-time purchases or that cost nothing to deliver.Home appliances, automotive (heated seats subscription), gaming (always-online DRM)
2.3.4Ad Injection into Paid TiersAdding advertising to previously ad-free tiers, then offering ad removal at a higher price.Streaming, gaming, smart-TV manufacturers
2.3.5Ad-Tier Bait-and-SwitchIntroducing a low-cost ad-supported tier whose ad load progressively increases over time.Streaming, podcasting
2.3.6Quality Throttling of Free TierDeliberately degrading the free or low-tier experience to manufacture urgency for upgrade.Dating (match visibility), gaming, e-commerce search, social media reach
2.3.7Microtransaction FatigueRequiring per-action payments (super likes, boosts, premium reactions) that accumulate beyond the advertised subscription cost.Dating, gaming (loot boxes), social media
2.3.8Grind-or-Pay DesignIntentionally slowing free progression to push players or users toward paid shortcuts.Gaming, dating

2.4 Vendor Lock-In · 10 practices

Autonomy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
2.4.1Proprietary-Format Lock-InStoring user data in proprietary formats with no documented open alternative, making migration prohibitively costly.Cloud/SaaS, healthcare (EHR), automotive (telematics), cybersecurity, music industry
2.4.2Data-Export ObstructionImposing technical or bureaucratic obstacles — throttled exports, mandatory tickets, complex transformations — that make leaving impractical.Cloud/SaaS, healthcare, freelance/gig platforms (portfolio export)
2.4.3Egress / Data-Out FeesSetting data-export or transfer fees far exceeding actual cost, financially penalizing departure.Cloud infrastructure, telecom (number porting fees)
2.4.4Punitive Early-Termination FeesImposing exit penalties that exceed the cost of staying, including full remaining-contract payment.Mobile carriers, cloud/SaaS, real estate, fitness, gym, waste management
2.4.5API Deprecation Without MigrationDeprecating APIs critical to customer integrations without providing migration paths, replacements, or adequate notice.Cloud/SaaS, social media, payment platforms
2.4.6Ecosystem Identity Lock-InRequiring use of the provider's identity, authentication, or management services across all products, making partial migration infeasible.Cloud/SaaS, search engines, AI platforms
2.4.7Parts Pairing / Component DRMUsing software locks or serialization that prevent third-party or self-installed parts from functioning even when physically compatible.Automotive, home appliances, agriculture (tractors), medical devices
2.4.8Carrier Unlock ObstructionMaintaining device locks beyond the contract period or imposing fees / bureaucracy to unlock paid-off devices.Mobile carriers
2.4.9Number Porting ObstructionDelaying, gating, or routing number-port requests through retention pressure to discourage carrier switching.Mobile carriers
2.4.10Open-Source Bait-and-SwitchBuilding market position on open-source releases, then transitioning core capabilities to proprietary or closed licenses once dominant.AI platforms, cloud/SaaS

Autonomy+ Fairness
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

2.5.2Mandatory Bundle PricingOffering only bundled packages that mix essential and optional items so individual costs cannot be compared.Funeral services, wedding planning, event ticketing, cable/internet

Autonomy+ Accountability
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

Autonomy+ Fairness
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

4.10 Data Sale to Brokers / Third Parties · 8 practices

Autonomy+ Privacy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
4.10.1Data Sale to BrokersSelling user, customer, patient, or worker data — including behavioral, demographic, and inferred attributes — to data brokers or downstream resellers.Cross-domain (healthcare, retail, telecom, social media, automotive, real estate, search, fitness, mental health, dating, education, music, entertainment, ride-hailing, food delivery, banking, advertising, dental, veterinary, alcohol, tobacco, supplements, prison, wedding, funeral, wedding, baby/children, senior care, firearms, etc.)
4.10.2Sensitive-Health Data SaleSelling mental health, reproductive, addiction, or therapy session data — including AI chatbot conversations — to advertisers or third parties.Mental health, pharma/biotech, dental, healthcare
4.10.3Therapy-Conversation HarvestingUsing AI mental health chatbot conversations for training, profiling, or sale without explicit consent.Mental health, AI
4.10.4Clinical-Trial Genetic Data SaleSelling or licensing genetic data collected from trial participants for secondary commercial use.Pharma/biotech
4.10.5Inmate Communication-Data SaleSelling or sharing inmate call records, purchases, or location data — extending surveillance to family members.Prison/corrections
4.10.6Loyalty-Program Data SaleSelling frequent-customer data — travel patterns, purchase histories, demographics — to insurers, marketers, or analytics firms.Airlines, hotels, retail, financial services
4.10.7Government-Agency Data SaleProviding personal data to law enforcement without warrants, exploiting commercial channels to bypass constitutional protections.Data brokers, surveillance technology
4.10.8Authoritarian-Regime SalesProviding data, analytics, surveillance, or imagery to governments with documented human rights abuses.Data brokers, AI, surveillance technology, space/aerospace (satellite imagery)

5.1 Consent Manipulation · 7 practices

Autonomy+ Privacy
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
5.1.1Bundled ConsentRequiring users to accept broad data collection, tracking, and analytics as a single all-or-nothing package rather than granular choices.Internal company ethics, social media, mobile apps

5.1.6Coerced Wearable / Telematics SharingConditioning meaningful discounts on sharing of wearable, driving, or other behavioral data, penalizing privacy-conscious customers.Insurance, automotive
5.1.7Genetic Data CoercionUsing or requesting genetic testing data for underwriting decisions or as a condition of service.Insurance
